_completeness.description: Reported response completeness, not a guarantee of complete platform history. Missing source assertions remain unknown.

data.description: Amazon responses include marketplace.country and marketplace.domain (resolved request marketplace, UK by default). X profiles preserve location, bio_link and cover_url when supplied. TikTok profiles preserve commerce_user, seller, region, location and business_category when supplied; region identifies the account region rather than personal residence. TikTok comments use platform_default selection, which can change between fetches; keep the same video and options when following cursors. Amazon review variant is readable text. Facebook profiles preserve cover_url, following and created_at when supplied; likes_count and followers are distinct and follower totals may be rounded. Endpoint-specific normalized payload, not one universal post/profile schema. Many lists use items/count/cursor; a null cursor means no usable next cursor was supplied, not proof that all history was retrieved. Check has_more and warnings where present. Social full-profile bundles use posts_cursor and posts_pagination.next_params; retain all returned next parameters. YouTube channel bundles instead use recent_videos, cursor and recent_videos_pagination. Inspect complete/partial/legs where supplied for bounded or failed components. Optional model-derived fields are labelled, not source facts.

stale.description: True only for an explicitly labelled, zero-credit reference snapshot served after a temporary upstream failure.

age_seconds.description: Age of a stale snapshot since its original retrieval; not reset by outage recovery.

fetched_at.description: Original retrieval time of a stale snapshot, in UTC.

synthetic.description: Present and true only on the explicitly requested /sandbox surface. Synthetic responses are representative and charged 0 credits; production /v1 never returns them.

degraded.description: Reserved for sandbox compatibility. Production /v1 reports upstream failure as an error and never serves a representative fallback.
